title: An Improved Mechanical Testing Method to Assess Bone-implant Anchorage
protocol: Manufacture rectangular implants from commercially pure titanium with dimensions 4 mm x 2.5 mm x 1.3 mm.
Drill a hole centrally down the long axis of each implant, diameter 0.7 mm.
Grit-blast the upper and lower surfaces to create a microtopographically complex surface.
Add calcium phosphate nanoparticles to half of the grit-blasted implants to create a nanotopographically complex surface.
Use young male Wistar rats (200-250 g) for the animal model.
Sedate rats using inhalation anesthesia: 4% isoflurane in 1 L O2/min for induction; 2% isoflurane in 1 L nitrous oxide and 0.6 L O2/min for maintenance.
Conduct a standard toe-pinch test to ensure effective sedation before continuing with the procedure.
Administer analgesic pre- and post-operatively through a subcutaneous injection of 0.01-0.05 mg/kg buprenorphine.
Assign implants bilaterally in the distal metaphyses of rat femora.
Shave and clean the antero-lateral aspect of each hind leg with 10% Betadine.
Place a warm water circulation pad underneath the anesthetized rat to prevent hypothermia.
Make an incision through the skin along the lateral aspect of the thigh using a #15 surgical scalpel.
Expose the distal femur using blunt dissection to deflect muscle bodies in a minimally invasive manner.
Scrape away the thin layer of periosteum overlying the femur using a periosteal elevator.
Drill a bicortical rectangular slot down the middle of the bone through both cortices, maintaining saline irrigation throughout drilling.
Drill through the anterior cortex using a 1.3 mm dental burr to create two holes 2.5 mm apart along the midline of the femur.
Extend these holes through the opposing cortex using a twist 1.3 mm dental burr, resulting in bicortical parallel holes.
Join the holes using a custom side-cutting burr in a proximal-distal direction, forming the site for the implant.
Pass a biodegradable suture through the bone defect using the attached needle and return around the outer femoral cortex.
Thread the implant over the free end of the suture and guide it into the defect, pressure-fitting it in place.
Orient the long axis of the implant perpendicular to the long axis of the femur.
Tie the suture around the lateral aspect of the femur to provide stability during recovery.
Use the remaining suture to close the muscle tissue.
Reoppose the cutaneous tissue using surgical staples.
Inspect surgical sites for signs of infection daily.
Monitor animals daily for compromised ambulatory ability.
Exclude animals that do not fully recover ambulation or have femoral fractures at sacrifice from analysis.
Sacrifice animals at 9 days post-operative by cervical dislocation after CO2 exposure.
Upon sacrifice, detach femora and clean of soft tissue.
Store detached femora immediately in 15% sucrose buffer solution to maintain tissue hydration.
Trim the bone to the width of the implants using a cylindrical diamond burr attached to a high speed system.
Remove any excess bony reparative callus growing around the long axis of the implant or into the longitudinal hole.
Assign a mechanical testing value of 0 N for arches that fall off during preparation or transportation.
Remove specimens from sucrose buffer solution.
Gently blot dry the specimens.
Position each specimen in the custom mold.
Slide the pin horizontally through holes in the walls of the mold and through the hole in the middle of the implant.
Place the stabilizing plate on the posterior side of the mold to stabilize the implant.
Fill the base of the mold with flowable dental composite.
Cure the dental composite for 60 seconds using a high intensity curing light.
After curing, open the mold and remove the hardened specimen block.
Draw a thin black line in permanent marker on the lateral arch for identification purposes.
Fix a prefabricated replica of the test specimen in a vice.
Center the unit on the base of the mechanical testing instrument.
Secure the specimen into vice.
Pass a nylon line through the hole in the implant.
Attach the loose ends to the center of the moving crosshead.
Label and test the lateral side first.
Repeat the process with the medial arch.
